findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Tagged on Wikimedia Commons with an anonymous public domain notice (Berne Convention Art. 7, >50 years since publication), accompanied by Commons' standard warning that anonymous PD status may not apply automatically in jurisdictions with longer anonymous or URAA terms (US, EU, India, Russia). Note also that English Wikipedia hosts a related local file File:Theresienstadt_film.jpg, whereas the verified Commons title is File:Theresienstadt_film_crew.jpg.

findings.claim: Candidate 10 (With Major Caveat) — Vedem Magazine Photograph on Wikimedia Commons (File:%C4%8Casopis_Vedem.jpg) vs. vedem-terezin.cz Scans
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: LOW CONFIDENCE for clean reuse: Although photographer Terezínská štafeta uploaded File:Časopis Vedem.jpg (5184×3456 px) as "Own work" under CC BY-SA 3.0 on April 5, 2013, the underlying 1942–1944 Vedem issues are cataloged at Terezín Memorial (Archiv Památníku Terezín A 1317), which explicitly claims all copyrights on vedem-terezin.cz, and several Vedem boys survived well past 1955 (e.g., Kurt Jiří Kotouč d. 2008, Zdeněk Taussig d. 2012). Do NOT use scans from vedem-terezin.cz (explicitly copyrighted by Památník Terezín), and treat File:Časopis Vedem.jpg with caution regarding underlying 2D content rights.

findings.claim: Exclusion / Do Not Use — Maurice Rossel 1944 ICRC Photographs & Restricted USHMM Items & Bundesarchiv Scope
findings.disagreements_or_caveats: Essential negative findings: (1) Maurice Rossel's June 23, 1944 photographs of Theresienstadt are NOT public domain; copyright is held by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC Audiovisual Archives, V-P-HIST series) and commercial/publication reuse requires prior express ICRC authorization (© International Committee of the Red Cross / Maurice Rossel / 1944). (2) USHMM collections.ushmm.org has mixed rights: researchers must verify "Rights & Restrictions" per record and only use records explicitly marked Public Domain (e.g. pa1121409), avoiding third-party/donor-restricted items. (3) Bundesarchiv's CC-BY-SA 3.0 DE Commons donation includes postwar 1963 Globke trial testimony photos of Theresienstadt survivors (e.g., File:Bundesarchiv Bild 183-B0711-0005-036, Oberstes Gericht, Globke-Prozess, Aussage, Judis Urbanova.jpg, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE, Attribution: "Bundesarchiv, Bild 183-B0711-0005-036 / CC-BY-SA 3.0"), not 1941–1945 camp photographs.
sources: ICRC Audiovisual Archives & ICRC Terms of Use
findings.value_or_range: Maurice Rossel (1944): Copyrighted by ICRC (DO NOT USE without ICRC license) | vedem-terezin.cz: Copyrighted by Terezín Memorial (DO NOT USE without permission) | USHMM: Mixed rights (use only explicit PD items like pa1121409) | Bundesarchiv CC BY-SA 3.0 DE: Postwar survivor testimony photos only (e.g. Globke-Prozess 1963)

myths_checked: Myth: Maurice Rossel's June 1944 Red Cross inspection photos of Theresienstadt are in the public domain because they are from WWII. Reality: Verified false — copyright is actively held by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), requiring prior express authorization for publication or commercial reuse.

Myth: All scans on vedem-terezin.cz or USHMM collections are public domain for open reuse. Reality: Verified false — vedem-terezin.cz explicitly states Památník Terezín retains all copyrights to texts and graphic scans (Archiv Památníku Terezín A 1317), and USHMM has mixed rights requiring per-record verification in the "Rights & Restrictions" block.

Myth: The Bundesarchiv Wikimedia Commons donation (CC BY-SA 3.0 DE) contains 1941–1945 wartime photographs of the Theresienstadt ghetto. Reality: Searches across Wikimedia Commons Bundesarchiv categories surface postwar 1963 Globke-Prozess survivor testimony photographs (e.g., Bild 183-B0711-0005-036 and -042), rather than wartime Bundesarchiv camp photography.

Myth: Any Wikimedia Commons file tagged "PD-anon" from 1942–1944 is unconditionally public domain everywhere. Reality: Commons explicitly flags anonymous 1942–1944 film stills (e.g. Shooting 'Film Ghetto Theresienstadt'.jpg and Theresienstadt film crew.jpg) with jurisdictional caveats regarding US URAA and EU term rules.
